item.title: Kayaking: Guided Paddle through the Sawmill Creek Wildlife Management Area — Sat Aug 8, 4:45 PM — Montclair Public Library
item.description:
Note: This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.
Known by many as the “Jewel of the Meadowlands,” the Sawmill Wildlife Management Area is the oldest protected wetlands in the NJ Meadowlands District - and is home to a remarkable variety of birds, fish and other wildlife. Before setting out in the company of experienced guides, students will receive a briefing conducted by a senior Hackensack Riverkeeper staff person who will explain the organization’s ongoing work and mission; and speak about some of the creatures you are most likely to encounter while on the water and in the wetlands.
PLEASE NOTE: We offer both single kayaks & tandem kayaks that fit two paddlers. These will be distributed on a first come, first served basis upon arrival at Laurel Hill Park.
If you need kayaking lessons ahead of the tour you can register for them individually through the Hackensack Riverkeepers.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.description:
Tech Toolbox is a free hands-on workshop series focused on building real, practical digital skills. Each session zeroes in on a specific skill, program, or tool—from core computer skills and file management to navigating software and online platforms you use every day. Participants are encouraged to bring their own devices and follow along, so you'll leave each session having actually practiced what you learned.
All experience levels are welcome, and your instructor will be there to walk you through everything step by step. Sessions are free and open to the public.

item.title: Tech Talks — Tue Aug 25, 3:30 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.
All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.

item.description:
Note: This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.
We will visit a different site each week to witness the southbound migration of birds from as far away as Alaska and the Russian Far East. Vireos, warblers, and tanagers are among the songbirds likely to be seen in August and September, along with a good range of wading birds. Our destinations will be set shortly before each excursion, the choice determined by recent reports of concentrations of migrants.

item.description:
THE JOURNEY OF PURA BELPRÉ’S TALES Pura Belpré was a talented author, collector of folktales, puppeteer and storyteller who wrote and reinterpreted Puerto Rican folk tales. Our show is a re-enactment of her legendary “Bilingual Story Hour” in a creative and interactive experience that combines storytelling with puppets!
El viaje de los cuentos de Pura Belpré Pura Belpré fue una talentosa escritora, coleccionista de cuentos tradicionales, titiritera y cuenta cuentos que escribió y re-interpretó las historias populares puertorriqueñas. Nuestro espectáculo es una recreación de su tradición de contar cuentos bilingües, en una experiencia creativa e inter- activa que combina el arte de contar cuentos con títeres
A REFORMA.ORG Noche de Cuentos grant funded event.

item.title: Classic Films Now: All the President’s Men — Sun Oct 25, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Run Time: 140 minutes. Recommended for ages 13+. A nation distrusts its institutions. News has become spectacle. Ordinary people fight to matter. Welcome to 1976. Academy Award winners Robert Redford and Dustin Hoffman star in this true story as Washington Post reporters Carl Bernstein and Bob Woodward, whose investigation of a seemingly minor hotel room break-in uncovers the greatest political scandal in United States history and leads to the downfall of President Richard Nixon.
Classic Films Now brings major works of cinema back to the big screen, films that not only defined their own time but continue to speak to ours. Each installment of the series gathers a group of landmark films curated around a theme, period, artist, or movement, inviting audiences to discover how the works connect with contemporary life. item.title: SMC Trail Work Volunteer Day — Sun Aug 2, 9:00 AM
item.description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group **TRAIL WORK will continue rerouting the Hogenauer Trail** up the slope and away from recently installed property fences. **Meet At:** Dog Park/ Wildflower Preserve, 11 Bear Lane, Maplewood. From there, we will walk to Crater View on Crest drive and then to the Hogenauer trail work site.
Trail work is physically challenging but very satisfying as we use hand tools to build and repair trails. Participants must be 15+ years. Those younger than 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Participants **should wear long pants** due to [ticks](https://www.somocon.org/?page_id=193928&fb) and thron bushes and sturdy shoes, and bring gloves (though backup gloves will be available). Tools, water, and a snack will be provided. (Registration is not required though if you sign up on Meetup, it helps us know how many tools to bring.) Only heavy, steady rain cancels.
Source: Meetup: South Mountain Conservancy

item.title: Movement, Strength, and Health Through Hormonal Change Workshop — Tue Sep 29, 1:30 PM — JCC MetroWest | Tepper Hall
item.description:
Learn how to move with confidence through perimenopause and menopause. This workshop explores how hormonal changes impact strength, energy, and recovery, and how to adapt your fitness routine to support bone health, muscle mass, and overall well-being. Leave with practical, sustainable strategies to feel strong and resilient at every stage. Led by Samantha Moir, PT, DPT, OCS, CSCS, a Board-Certified Orthopedic Physical Therapist, Certified Strength and Conditioning Specialist, and Certified Tennis Performance Trainer. Free and open to the public / Registration required Register
For more information: Ellen Robertson, erobertson@jccmetrowest.org or (973) 530-3415.

item.description:
Are you interested in exploring the monthly themes through writing and sharing with others? The purpose of this group is to write about the monthly theme before the meeting and share your writing with the group. item.title: Lego Robotics for Elementary Students — Sat Aug 1, 1:00 PM — RecRoom
item.description: LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. Kids will explore: • Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components • Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect) • Testing, debugging, and iterating designs • Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas Details: • 60-minute session • Small-group format • No prior experience required Community Spons
